# Phase 68.2: SDK-Owned Read Chain and Resolved Folder Listings - Discussion Log

> **Audit trail only.** Do not use as input to planning, research, or execution agents.
> Decisions are captured in CONTEXT.md — this log preserves the alternatives considered.

**Date:** 2026-07-06
**Phase:** 68.2-sdk-owned-read-chain-and-resolved-folder-listings
**Areas discussed:** Read-listing API shape, Freshness policy, Anti-rollback gate reuse, Cutover sequencing

---

## Read-listing API shape

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| `listFolder()` + events → Zustand projection | Imperative `client.listFolder()`/`listSharedFolder()` → `ResolvedChild[]` + `folder:updated` event; `folder.store.ts` a thin projection. Matches existing client patterns + SC#3. | ✓ |
| SDK-owned reactive store | SDK owns an observable store the web mirrors 1:1; new pattern, no precedent. | |
| React Query over SDK resolve | Web wraps SDK resolve in useQuery; RQ cache holds listings — reintroduces a second cache (tension w/ SC#2/#3). | |
| You decide | Defer to planner. | |

**User's choice:** `listFolder()` + events → projection (recommended)
**Notes:** Aligns with SC#3 (single owner = SDK `folderTree`).

---

## Freshness policy (the desync fix — SC#5)

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Re-resolve on every folder open/nav | No stale cache across nav; cache per-view; existing 30s poll stays. Deterministic SC#5 fix. | |
| Poll-driven invalidation only | Poll detects seq bump → invalidate; nav uses cache; up to ~30s staleness. | |
| Nav re-resolve + poll invalidation (belt-and-suspenders) | Fresh on nav AND poll-driven invalidation for the open folder. Most live. | ✓ |
| You decide | Defer to planner. | |

**User's choice:** Nav re-resolve + poll invalidation (belt-and-suspenders)
**Notes:** Nav-resolve leg is the deterministic SC#5 fix; poll leg keeps an open folder live.

---

## Anti-rollback gate reuse (Gate / boundary)

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Reuse `RotationHighWater` as the single gated entrypoint | Route the read-listing resolve through existing `RotationHighWater.enforceResolved`; raw sdk-core resolve internal-only; no new abstraction. | ✓ (via follow-up) |
| Introduce a distinct `DurableFloorStore` | New adapter per roadmap wording; risk of two floor stores drifting. | |
| You decide | Defer to researcher. | |

**User's choice:** "Other" — freeform architectural directive: *"Ideally the web ui should not be doing any raw resolves or ipfs/ipns accesses or any calls to sdk-core. the entire reason for the existence of the sdk is to mediate this."*
**Notes:** Reframed the gate question into a boundary principle. Two plain-text follow-ups resolved it:
1. Confirmed reuse of the existing `RotationHighWater`/`HighWaterStore` seam as the "DurableFloorStore" (no new abstraction); user added that `HighWaterStore` must be mocked/injected for Node.js SDK unit tests.
2. On boundary scope, user directed that the **write path be included in this phase too** — "phase 69 is entirely Rust/Desktop side and should not be conflated with the current TS code (web + sdk)." Orchestrator clarified (accepted, subject to user review) that the boundary targets **runtime** sdk-core/core calls + raw IPFS/IPNS; **type-only imports remain allowed** to avoid a ~54-file no-op churn.

---

## Cutover sequencing / risk

| Option | Description | Selected |
|--------|-------------|----------|
| Big-bang, web-e2e-gated, revert mirror last | Build API + gated resolve → desync web-e2e → rewire + delete web dupes → revert `ba3e0229a` mirror last. Full suite green. | ✓ |
| Incremental behind a fallback flag | Land API alongside existing path behind a flag; temporary dual state (against SC#3). | |
| Revert mirror first, then build | Remove mirror up front; risks a size/modified display gap mid-phase. | |
| You decide | Defer to planner. | |

**User's choice:** Big-bang, web-e2e-gated, revert mirror last (recommended)

---

## Claude's Discretion

- Wave/plan decomposition and granularity.
- Exact `ResolvedChild` field naming + `folder:updated` event payload shape; whether/where the SDK re-exports read-schema types for the web.
- Internal SDK cache structure + invalidation wiring (keyed by IPNS name; `sequenceNumber` is the clock).
- Whether owned vs shared listing share one internal resolver or two thin wrappers.

## Deferred Ideas

- Rust/FUSE/WinFsp SDK-owned read chain (Phase 68.2 parity) → Phase 69 (Rust side only; not conflated with TS).
- Codec/crypto redesign, frozen-schema changes → out of milestone scope.
- 68.1 gap-closure round-2 write-plane bugs remain owned by the open Phase 68.1 block (re-check overlap before planning if 68.1 closes first).
- sdk/sdk-core write-plane dedup + terminology renames reviewed but not folded (touch opportunistically only).
